projects.name: AllyLab
projects.summary: An accessibility review workflow across a React dashboard, API and CLI, with a companion Next.js website.
projects.contribution: I built AllyLab’s accessibility review workflow across a React dashboard, API and CLI, and its companion Next.js website. The interface connects automated findings with AI-assisted suggestions and human review.
projects.outcome: The implementation includes selection, filtering and finding-detail tests, plus rescan utilities that check whether rule IDs remain. The result connects a reported issue to a reviewable change.

projects.evidenceLabel: Real application · guided still sequence · synthetic findings and metrics · no API or model calls.

story.name: AllyLab
story.title: From findings to reviewable fixes.
story.summary: An accessibility review workflow across a React dashboard, API and CLI, with a companion Next.js website.
story.alt: AllyLab findings table with severity, recurring status and four synthetic accessibility findings
story.problemTitle: A finding needs a next step.
story.problem: An accessibility finding is only the beginning. Engineers need to understand its severity, track its status, inspect a suggested change and verify what remains.
story.contributionTitle: Connect the finding to engineering work.
story.contribution: I built AllyLab’s accessibility review workflow across a React dashboard, API and CLI, and its companion Next.js website. The interface connects automated findings with AI-assisted suggestions and human review.
story.decisionTitle: Separate urgency, lifecycle and loading cost.
story.decision: Severity and issue status remain separate because urgency and lifecycle answer different questions. Reporting views load on demand, with chart and export code separated from the initial loading path.
story.tradeoff: Deferred screens need explicit loading states. Structured suggestions remain proposals for human review. No bundle-size or load-time improvement is claimed here.

flow.title: Finding
flow.body: Scan output identifies the rule, severity and affected interface.

flow.title: Suggested change
flow.body: Structured AI-assisted suggestions connect proposed code to the finding.

flow.title: Review + rescan
flow.body: Inspect the change and check whether the rule remains.

steps.title: Review findings
steps.body: Four synthetic findings keep severity and lifecycle status separate. These sample findings illustrate interface states, not accessibility results for a real customer.
steps.alt: Real AllyLab findings table with four synthetic issues and separate severity and status columns

steps.title: Filter by severity
steps.body: Selecting Critical narrows the table to the missing-alt finding. The score and scan time visible in this fixture are synthetic, not measured performance.
steps.alt: Critical filter selected in AllyLab with one missing-alt finding visible

steps.title: Inspect the finding
steps.body: The detail panel exposes the rule, selector and source element. The fixture has no element screenshot, so the real interface shows its empty state. Generate AI Fix was not activated.
steps.alt: AllyLab finding detail panel with rule, CSS selector, HTML element and an explicit missing screenshot state

story.captureBoundary: Real application · guided still sequence · synthetic findings and metrics · no API or model calls.
story.outcome: The implementation includes selection, filtering and finding-detail tests, plus rescan utilities that check whether rule IDs remain. The result connects a reported issue to a reviewable change.
story.limits: A suggested fix still needs review. Automated checks and rescanning do not certify accessibility or establish a measured accessibility outcome.

projects.contribution: I built Conductor to organize agent work into tracks with dependencies and task-specific Markdown context. Its planning interface makes those relationships visible before execution.
projects.outcome: The implementation validates declared dependencies, detects cycles and schedules using dependsOn. The captured interface makes the relationship between two prerequisites and a review track readable.

story.name: Conductor
story.title: Make the dependencies visible.
story.summary: Tracks, dependencies and task-specific context make parallel agent work easier to inspect before execution.
story.alt: Conductor graph showing Review interface dependent on Component system and Retrieval API
story.problemTitle: Parallel work still needs an order.
story.problem: Agent work needs an explicit plan: which tasks can start, which depend on another track, and what context belongs to each task.
story.contributionTitle: Give each track its own context.
story.contribution: I built Conductor to organize agent work into tracks with dependencies and task-specific Markdown context. Its planning interface makes those relationships visible before execution.
story.decision: A track carries its own context and dependencies instead of relying on one undifferentiated conversation. The scheduler checks the dependency graph before starting work, including dependency-cycle detection.
story.tradeoff: The plan is only as useful as the dependencies and context supplied to it. Describing scope in context is not proof of permission enforcement.

flow.title: Define tracks
flow.body: Give each task a goal, context and declared dependencies.

flow.title: Resolve dependencies
flow.body: Validate the graph and detect cycles before scheduling.

flow.title: Schedule eligible work
flow.body: Start work according to dependency readiness.

steps.title: Prerequisites
steps.body: Component system and Retrieval API are separate prerequisite tracks in this synthetic example.

steps.title: Dependency
steps.body: Review interface depends on both prerequisites. The graph makes that relationship inspectable.

steps.title: Execution boundary
steps.body: This capture shows planning only. No agent workers executed, so the graph is not evidence of successful delivery.

story.captureBoundary: Real local planning interface · three synthetic tracks · no workers executed.
story.outcome: The implementation validates declared dependencies, detects cycles and schedules using dependsOn. The captured interface makes the relationship between two prerequisites and a review track readable.
story.limits: This demonstrates planning, not agent delivery, reliability metrics or employer adoption.

projects.name: Evalgate
projects.summary: Markdown work contracts connect acceptance criteria to executable checks and visible results.
projects.contribution: I built Evalgate to connect Markdown work contracts to executable checks, record their results, and leave failed checks unresolved for inspection and an explicit retry.
projects.outcome: The CLI parses pending contracts, runs their verifiers, prints failure output and updates the Markdown using the results. In the sample run, the failed source-evidence contract remains pending.
projects.imageAlt: Evalgate contract cards showing two passed checks and a missing-evidence check remaining pending
projects.evidenceLabel: Real local sample execution · two passed · one deliberate failure · synthetic checks.

story.name: Evalgate
story.title: Keep the failure evidence.
story.summary: Markdown work contracts connect acceptance criteria to executable checks and visible results.
story.alt: Evalgate contract cards showing two passed checks and a missing-evidence check remaining pending
story.problem: An agent reporting completion does not establish that a task met its acceptance criteria. The result needs an inspectable check.
story.contributionTitle: Connect the contract to the check.
story.contribution: I built Evalgate to connect Markdown work contracts to executable checks, record their results, and leave failed checks unresolved for inspection and an explicit retry.
story.decision: Define a verifier alongside the task and use its result to update completion. Shell and HTTP checks test explicit conditions; model-based judgment carries different uncertainty.
story.tradeoff: A passing check proves only the property it tested. Retries are explicit and the declared retry count is advisory. JSON checks cover a limited shape; file-pattern checks are not a semantic-diff engine.

flow.title: Define acceptance
flow.body: Write the task and the executable property to verify.

flow.title: Run verifier
flow.body: Evaluate the condition and retain its output.

flow.title: Accept or retain failure
flow.body: Update passing contracts; leave failures unresolved for inspection.

steps.title: Passed checks
steps.body: Two synthetic checks passed in the real local sample run. These are illustrative results, not a performance benchmark.

steps.title: Missing evidence
steps.body: The deliberately missing source-evidence check failed. Its contract stays pending instead of claiming completion.

steps.title: Review and retry
steps.body: Read the failure output before an explicit retry. A plausible answer does not replace missing evidence.

story.captureBoundary: Real local sample execution · two passed · one deliberate failure · synthetic checks.
story.outcome: The CLI parses pending contracts, runs their verifiers, prints failure output and updates the Markdown using the results. In the sample run, the failed source-evidence contract remains pending.
story.limits: Sample results are demonstration evidence, not product performance metrics. Passing checks do not prove unchecked properties.

teaching.title: Teach the practice. Review the work.
teaching.summary: At Oracle, I developed an AI engineering playbook and delivered practical training on AI fundamentals, prompts, APIs, agents and engineering best practices.
teaching.scope: The public exercise is an original recreated example. It is not an Oracle document or evidence that every topic was delivered there.

exercise.title: A plausible answer still needs evidence.
exercise.prompt: Given only the supplied source, return a summary and a source identifier. If the source does not establish the answer, return insufficient_evidence.
exercise.failure: A response can match the expected JSON shape while citing a source that does not exist.
criteria: Validate the response shape at the API boundary.
Check that the cited identifier exists in the supplied source set.
Keep missing evidence unresolved rather than inventing a citation.
Use human review to assess whether the source actually supports the summary.
exercise.limits: An original public exercise using isolated synthetic fixtures. No model calls or employer code. The gate checks shape and source existence; a human must assess whether the source supports the answer.
exercise.result: Four deterministic fixtures produced the expected outcomes: existing source → ready for review; invented citation → missing source; explicit missing evidence → needs review; malformed response → invalid shape.

rag.summary: Private RAG work combines embeddings, scoped retrieval, structured generation, streaming and citations.
rag.boundary: Public explanations use synthetic data. Any scripted demonstration makes no model calls and does not expose private code or records.

architecture.title: Completion follows the verifier
architecture.constraint: An agent report is not acceptance evidence.
architecture.decision: Run an explicit verifier and retain its output.
architecture.result: Passing contracts update; failures remain pending for inspection and explicit retry.
architecture.scope: Source-verified implementation pattern; sample outcomes are illustrative. A pass covers only the checked property.
